summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood (AE+SE) and Orion GPU Systems to explore go-to-market alignment and technical integration options. Discussed deployment modes (hosted vs private/VPC vs on-prem), perf targets for inference workloads, KV cache/batching behavior, KMS and SOC2, and a proposed benchmarking window. Agreed next steps: share security docs and partner packet, schedule SE deep dive and benchmarking.
topics: technical integration options (private deployment, VPC, on-prem)
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-08-20 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Alvarez (Redwood SE), James Patel (Orion Partnerships), Erin Zhao (Orion Product), Carlos Mendes (Orion Hardware Eng)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we can get started. I'm Maya, I'll lead the partner motion on our side, and with me is Leo, our lead solutions engineer.
[00:12] James (Orion): Hey Maya, hey Leo, James here. Thanks for setting this up. Super interested in hearing how Redwood sees partners like us fitting in.
[00:20] Maya: Yeah, totally. Quick agenda — just do intros, a bit of GTM alignment, then dig into the technical bits that matter for your infra, perf and security, and finish with next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Erin (Orion): Works for me.
[00:35] Leo (Redwood SE): Cool. Maybe I'll kick into the technical overview quick — high level, Redwood runs across hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private deployments (VPC / on-prem). We optimize for low-latency inference with batching, KV cache, and per-model kernel selection.
[00:50] Carlos (Orion): When you say private can you be more concrete? Like, are we talking a control plane in your cloud with data plane in our VPC, or fully on-prem boxed appliances?
[01:05] Leo: Good question — both patterns exist. We offer a private control plane model where control plane sits with Redwood and the inference nodes run in your VPC via connectors; we also support a fully air-gapped on-prem package for regulated customers. There are tradeoffs — maintenance, SLOs, and support model differ.
[01:25] James: Ok that helps. Our angle is we build GPU hardware and also want to enable channel partnerships where we can offer a combined stack. So understanding the lift and the technical integration points is key.
[01:35] Maya: Makes sense. On the GTM side — we typically do co-marketing, joint benchmarks, and partner referrals. For channel economics we have a rev-share model we can map out after technical fit.
[01:45] Erin: On benchmarks, what's typical — do you run per-customer workloads or generic LLM benchmarks? We care about tail-latency on 2-4k token sequences for a few of our reference models.
[01:58] Leo: We do both. For initial evals we run standardized throughput/latency tests (gen-100/512/2k etc), then customer-specific workloads. Tail latency depends a lot on batching and KV cache hit patterns — for 2-4k tokens you often need tuned kernel paths and sometimes sequence-slicing to avoid memory blowouts.
[02:20] Carlos: Sequence-slicing — do you mean you chunk the request or do you stream partial outputs to maintain latency?
[02:28] Leo: We use a combination. Streaming helps user-perceived latency. For model internals, when sequences get long we optimize attention memory and use runtime kernels that reduce peak memory. Also quantization profiles can change memory/latency tradeoffs.
[02:40] James: Speaking of quantization, are you advising partners on which quant formats to support? Our HW is optimized for INT8 on certain architectures.
[02:50] Leo: Yes, our Optimize toolkit provides suggestions by workload. For partners we can share quantization profiles and supported formats; we'll also map model variants to recommended hw profiles. There may be some artifacts — e.g., small accuracy deltas with extreme quantization — we monitor that with evals.
[03:05] Erin: From a systems standpoint, how do you handle model fallbacks? If the customer's deployed model isn't available do you have automatic fallbacks to a lower-capacity variant?
[03:15] Leo: Yes, smart routing rules let you fallback by policy — region, cost tier, or compatible model variant. That helps maintain availability during capacity spikes.
[03:23] James: Security — SOC 2 is table stakes for many of our customers, and we also need KMS integration and audit logs. Do you support HSM/KMS and SAML SSO?
[03:35] Maya: We do. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and we have SOC2 docs; SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported via our console. We'll share the SOC2 report and a partner security packet after this call.
[03:50] Carlos: Good. Also curious about networking — egress, NAT, and if you'll need direct peering for low latency.
[03:58] Leo: For VPC deployments you control egress. For dedicated and hosted we recommend region co-location and peering where possible. We can work with your network team on specific topology; often a direct connect or peered setup reduces hop count and tail latency.
[04:15] James: Great. On the partner integration side, what APIs or SDKs do you expose for resellers vs co-managed customers?
[04:25] Maya: API is the same for most customers — REST and SDKs for Python/Node. For partners we add a partner-level API for provisioning and usage metering. For channel resellers we have program docs that detail provisioning flows.
[04:36] Erin: Are there limits on model variants or how many concurrent dedicated pools a partner can provision?
[04:44] Leo: Limits are configurable. For Dedicated we reserve capacity per commit. For Private deployments it's more about hardware footprint — we can scale horizontally.
[04:51] James: Pricing is an open question obviously — we want to know how margins could work if we bundle HW plus Redwood.
[04:58] Maya: Totally — we'll share a starter rev-share and pricing doc after tech fit. Usually partners get preferential dedicated pricing for bundled offers.
[05:06] Speaker 1 (generic): [interruption] sorry can you repeat the part about KV cache?
[05:10] Leo: Sure, KV cache is a runtime optimization storing past key/value states so repeated prefixes don't re-compute. Partners with recurring chat-like workloads see big per-token cost reductions. Hit rate depends on prompt patterns and app architecture.
[05:27] Carlos: For our hardware validation, can you run microbenchmarks that show GPU utilization and power draw for a given model mix? We need that to size our blades.
[05:36] Leo: Yes, we can run perf traces and GPU profiler outputs during benchmarks. We'll need controlled workload scripts; ideally you provide model binaries and configs or we pick close-match open models.
[05:49] James: Timeline — what's reasonable for a proof-of-concept and a pilot?
[05:55] Maya: Usually a 2-week benchmark window followed by a 4-8 week pilot depending on integration complexity. So end-to-end could be 8-12 weeks to first joint offering if both teams prioritize.
[06:07] Erin: That aligns. One more Q — for on-prem installs, who handles upgrades and patching, and what's the SLA?
[06:16] Leo: For fully on-prem we offer an ops package where Redwood handles upgrades and support with a light agent, or customers can self-manage with our update bundles. SLA varies with commercial tier; we can provide details in the partner packet.
[06:27] James: Sounds good. Any regulatory concerns for telco customers — data residency?
[06:33] Maya: We support region controls and private deployments; for telco or regulated customers we recommend private or on-prem to meet residency and audit requirements.
[06:40] Carlos: Minor note — sometimes model names get garbled in your docs, we've seen 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'Redwood Delayed' in a PDF, lol.
[06:48] Maya: [laughs] noted. We're used to transcription oddities.
[06:52] Leo: Back to benchmarks — can we tentatively book the week of Sep 1 for a perf window? That gives us two weeks to prepare scripts.
[06:59] James: I can confirm after I sync with hardware ops, but please tentatively schedule.
[07:05] Erin: Also we'll want to loop in our sales ops to discuss co-selling rules.
[07:12] Maya: Great. We'll send a partner checklist and SOC2/KMS docs. Leo will follow up with a benchmark plan and required artifacts.
[07:20] James: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:23] Maya: Quick recap — Redwood to send partner one-pager and security docs; SE to send benchmark plan; Orion to confirm availability for week of Sep 1. We'll propose next meeting: technical deep dive mid next week.
[07:36] Carlos: Thanks all. Looking forward to the materials.
[07:40] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[07:43] End of transcript.

Notes: transcription includes small mis-hearings and occasional speaker label glitches; timestamps approximate. References shared: "partner one-pager" (to be attached), SOC2 report (to be shared via secure link), benchmark scripts (SE deliverable).
